query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

generation.hypothesis: The single intervention of utilizing machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations with a carefully curated dataset of high-entropy alloys can overcome the limitations in determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states
generation.mechanism: The machine learning algorithm learns patterns in the molecular dynamics simulations, allowing for accurate predictions of thermodynamic properties across various compositions and temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved accuracy, availability, and efficiency in determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties compared to current experimental and computational baselines
generation.baseline: Current experimental and computational methods for determining thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys
generation.boundary: Applicable to high-entropy alloys with 3-10 principal elements, temperatures between 500-2000 K
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of the machine learning model, potential limitations in the dataset used for training, and the complexity of the high-entropy alloy systems

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of predicted thermodynamic properties from machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations with independent experimental reference data
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted values deviate from the experimental reference data by more than 10%, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: To overcome twenty-first century grand engineering challenges, the investigation of unexplored central region of the ternary phase diagram is indispensable, which occupies the complex multi-component alloys or popularly known high-entropy alloys (HEAs),. HEAs have ample compositional space and possess exceptional properties such as excellent mechanical performance at high temperatures, exceptional ductility, high fracture toughness at cryogenic temperatures, bio-compatibility, high conductivity, excellent catalytic and magnetic properties which means that one or more than one HEA can potentially offer a solution for most engineering problems concerning materials. The combination theory suggests a large compositional space (nearly ~ 108 types of HEAs can be developed from about 64 elements in the periodic table) in the central region of the ternary phase diagram,. However, it is only since 2004 when HEAs were first discovered, and since then, the profound study is compelling to accelerate the pace of discovery of novel HEAs. The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. The improved melting behavior of high-entropy compounds by the addition of nitrogen provides a promising way towards modification of thermal properties of functional and constructional materials.

The melting temperature together with supercooling and superheating temperatures of a number of high-entropy carbonitrides (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x with different concentrations of carbon substituted by nitrogen are calculated. The deep learning DeepMD potential is trained on the number of DFT calculations in order to accurately describe both the liquid and solid phases of the considered high-entropy carbonitrides. A new computational procedure is developed and applied to determine the melting hysteresis and melting temperature of HECN using active learning techniques. Heating and cooling curves for HECNs are calculated and carefully analyzed in order to determine the main trends in changes of melting temperatures with respect to nitrogen content. Pair correlation analysis is employed to explain the enhancement of the melting temperature of carbonitrides with small amounts of nitrogen. The obtained data indicates the potential of applications of high-entropy carbonitrides as promising hard and refractive materials for protective coatings of various equipment which operates at extreme conditions.

Unlike traditional alloys based on one or two principal elements, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) employ five or more elements in relatively high concentrations (5-35 at.%), with an original picture that the maximum configuration entropy engenders the formation of single-phase solid solution,. Since its inception, this state-of-the-art class of alloys has become the “fertile playground” to explore superior mechanical properties benefits,, such as high strength, excellent resistance to fatigue and fracture,, and strong wear resistance, because of their untraditional compositions and chemical structures. In particular, the intrinsic complex interactions among multi-principal components, mainly tied to mixing entropy ΔSmix, mixing enthalpy ΔHmix, atomic size difference δ, electronegativity difference χ, and valence electron concentration (VEC), render the compositional space of high-entropy family vast and uncharted,; it provides enough opportunities for diverse structural heterogeneity topologically and/or chemically through contemplating elements selection with appropriate numbers, species, and concentrations,.
